title: Ops velocity: sprint handback and SLO digest (2027-04-19)
content:
Purpose:
This note captures the weekly handback from the operations sprint (2027-04-12 -> 2027-04-18), plus a concise SLO digest, incidents summary, and explicit handoff items for the on-call rotation starting 04/20. Use this as the single source for the Monday standup and for preparing the runbook edits.

Quick summary highlights:
- Service velocity: deployment cadence increased to 6 deploys/day (stable channels); rollback rate 0.7% (one automatic rollback due to OOM on a quantized worker).
- SLO picture: overall hosted-api availability 99.96% (region-us-west), latency regressions detected on p95 for short sequences (<= 64 tokens) Tuesday morning spike.
- Incidents: one P1 (INC-2027-0142) affecting short-sequence generation (5-20 tokens) between 09:12–09:46 on 2027-04-13; circuit breaker tripped on a single autoscale pool.
- Actionable: three runbook edits, two immediate mitigation tactics, one follow-up postmortem assigned.

Incidents (concise):
1) INC-2027-0142 — short-sequence token perf spike (P1)
   - Window: 2027-04-13 09:12 -> 09:46 UTC
   - Impact: elevated p95 latency on hosted-api text-generation for sequences <= 64 tokens; spike seen only in us-west region; customer-facing error rate remained low (<0.2% increase).
   - Detection: automated SLO alert (p95 latency > 220ms for 10m).
   - Immediate mitigation applied: throttled background batcher for quantized-llama models and forced fallback to non-quantized nodes for critical pods. Circuit breaker prevented broader cascade.
   - Root cause (hypothesis): combination of a kernel selection edge-case in the runtime when sequence length distribution shifted (heavy short sequences) plus a concurrent autoscale cold-start policy that created IO pressure on NVMe-backed cache layer.
   - Owners: triage lead Ethan Morales; mitigation run by oncall rotation A (Liu Zhang); postmortem lead assigned to Priya Nair (JIRA: JIRA-OPS-1423).

2) Minor incident — disk pressure on dedupe-cache (2027-04-15)
   - Resolved by emergency LRU eviction and increasing cache grace size in the config; follow-up: add healthcheck to evict earlier before eviction stalls service.

SLO snapshot (week ending 2027-04-18):
- Hosted API availability (region-us-west): 99.96% (target 99.95%) — on target but trending flat.
- p95 latency (text-gen, seq<=64): 238ms (target < 220ms) — regression window: Tuesday 09:00–10:30.
- p99 latency (all sequences): 840ms (target < 900ms) — healthy.
- Error rate (5xx): 0.18% (target <0.5%) — healthy.
Notes: the p95 regression is the highest priority metric this week; instrumentation traces indicate queuing on inference workers rather than model compute time.

On-call handoff (what the next rotation needs to know):
- Current status: mitigation for INC-2027-0142 is in place (fallback routing + temporary throttles). Postmortem in progress; no ongoing customer escalations.
- Runbooks to consult (updated sections):
  - "short-sequence perf spike" (new section added, see linked Confluence page)
  - "autoscale-cold-start diagnostics" (minor edits needed to include NVMe pressure indicators)
- Immediate triage checklist (for oncall):
  1. If p95 > 240ms for >15m: escalate to triage lead and enable manual fallback to non-quantized pool for affected routes.
  2. If error rate >0.5%: run smoke tests (smoke-suite/v2) and inspect worker OOM/kube events.
  3. If disk pressure alerts fire for dedupe-cache: trigger emergency eviction and notify infra (Slack #infra-storage).
- Contacts: infra-stability (pager duty) -> Carlos Ruiz; runtime-engineering -> Maya Patel; platform-observability -> Robin Kim.

Runbook and docs changes (this sprint):
- Added: "short-sequence perf spike" with triage steps + automated remediation toggles.
- Edited: autoscale doc to surface NVMe-backed cache pressure signals and recommended scaling headroom (increase cache headroom from 15% to 25% for quantized pools).
- TODO: draft a small playbook for coordinated fallback (routing + cache eviction) — owner: Liu Zhang (JIRA-OPS-1436).

Action items / sprint carryover (high priority):
- JIRA-OPS-1423 (Priya) — Postmortem for INC-2027-0142. Deliverable: RCA and mitigation plan by 2027-04-26.
- JIRA-OPS-1436 (Liu) — Implement coordinated fallback playbook, test in staging by 2027-04-29.
- JIRA-OPS-1440 (Ethan) — Add NVMe pressure metrics to platform observability and set an alert threshold; target: 2027-04-23.
- JIRA-OPS-1451 (Maya) — Runbook edits to autoscale policy; include suggested headroom and a canary traffic pattern. Target: 2027-04-22.
- Quick win: add an ad-hoc probe that sends 32-token synthetic requests every 2 minutes to exercise short-path kernels (owner: Carlos, due 2027-04-21).

Meeting notes (standup/triage 2027-04-19):
- Triage review: agreed kernel selection bug is plausible; runtime team to reproduce with a short-seq-heavy workload.
- Observability: added a temporary dashboard for short-seq p50/p95/p99 and queue depth per worker.
- Release cadence: pause non-critical deploys for 24h if p95 stays > 230ms.

Backlog & priorities for next sprint:
- Stabilize short-path kernels and add unit/integration tests for sequence-length heuristics. (High)
- Improve autoscale cold-start behavior: pre-warm NVMe cache on scale-up events (Medium).
- Expand synthetic short-seq probes across regions (Low -> quick win if small infra cost).

Decisions required:
- Do we increase cache headroom for quantized pools permanently? (ops + infra decision)
  - Proposal: increase to 25% for 2 weeks while we validate. Pros: reduces emergency evictions; cons: increases reserved storage.
- Approve creation of a short-seq synthetic probe pipeline (budget ~ $300/mo).

Notes to self / informal bits:
- Keep the postmortem lightweight — focus on triggers and measurable mitigations (no speculative design sections).
- Remember to link the kernel repro PR once we have a deterministic test case (call out to runtime team on Monday).
- Slack thread: #ops-bridge has the triage timeline; pin the postmortem doc when ready.

Attachments / artifacts:
- Confluence: short-sequence perf spike doc (linked above).
- JIRA: JIRA-OPS-1423 (postmortem), JIRA-OPS-1436 (playbook), JIRA-OPS-1440 (observability).
- Incident timeline (raw): available in INC-2027-0142 ticket.

Unresolved questions
- Did the runtime change in the last two weeks include any kernel-selection heuristics that would re-order branches for short sequences? (runtime-engineering owns answer)
- Was there a correlated spike in traffic from any specific enterprise customer? Need to check request metadata logs.

If you're the oncall starting 2027-04-20:
- Read the new short-seq runbook before 09:00 UTC.
- Keep the rollback threshold handy (p95 > 240ms for 15m).
- Reach out to Priya (owner) if anything beyond mitigation shows persistent recurrence.

-- Priya
